decision: SCOPE -> W3: hunt first. The hunt FOUND a page whose sentence names nectarine: unh_ext 'Growing Peaches and Nectarines in the Home Garden' (PDF) "Plant peach and nectarine trees 12 to 15 feet apart." -> in_row [144,180]. CONFIRMED 2026-10-01: (a) the sentence itself names nectarine, not only the title; (b) it is for STANDARD trees: the same page says 'Dwarf peach trees aren't recommended as dwarfing rootstocks for peaches are not reliably hardy in New Hampshire', and no trained form (espalier, hedgerow) is described; the figure is a cold-climate home-garden standard-tree spacing; no row figure (not_authored). UIUC's home-garden table ('Peach, Apricot. Nectarine, Plum | Seedling (standard) | 14 x 20 to 20 x 28', in-row 14-20 ft) corroborates the lower band. UGA C1063 (peaches, 18-20 ft; today's figure) is the sibling page and is not accepted since the hunt succeeded. Clemson peaches-nectarines carries no tree spacing (verified live). A notable move: 18-20 ft -> 12-15 ft. The 12 scanner hits are fruit-thinning distances (one fruit every 6 to 8 inches): agrees. EVIDENCE NOTE: the page is a PDF; the manifest hashes the raw bytes and the quote is checked against pypdf's text extraction of those bytes (ruled 2026-10-01; PDF_TEXT_EXTRACTOR pins pypdf 6.14.2).
